article.title: Hit the books
article.description: Meaning: to study hard, usually before an exam. Example: 'I can't go out tonight, I need to hit the books for tomorrow's test.' Register: informal, common among students. Similar idiom: 'cram for an exam' (study intensively at the last minute).
article.content: Meaning: to study hard, usually before an exam. Example: 'I can't go out tonight, I need to hit the books for tomorrow's test.' Register: informal, common among students. Similar idiom: 'cram for an exam' (study intensively at the last minute).

generated.caption:
Feeling the pressure before a big test? Then it's time to "hit the books"! This informal idiom means to study hard, usually for an exam. For example: "I can't go out tonight, I need to hit the books for tomorrow's test." Perfect for when you need to focus!

generated.script: Exam time mein 'bahut padhna hai' ko English mein kaise bole? Sirf 'study hard' nahi, there's a cooler idiom for that. Woh idiom hai 'Hit the books'. Iska matlab hai to study hard, usually exam se pehle. Ye especially students ke beech bahut common aur informal hai. Jaise, "I can't go out tonight, I need to hit the books for tomorrow's test." Dekha, kitna easy hai! Toh ab jab bhi exams se pehle dil laga ke padhai karni ho na, toh bolo 'I need to hit the books'. Ab samajh aaya? Comment karke batao aapko ye idiom pata tha ya nahi! slides.body: When someone tells you to 'hit the books,' they're encouraging you to study hard, usually in preparation for an upcoming exam. This informal idiom is very common among students. For example, you might say, 'I can't go out tonight, I need to hit the books for tomorrow's test.' It's similar to 'cram for an exam,' which also means to study intensively, often at the last minute.
